item.text: {"text":"The closest direct match is [2Gated-TimeGRU (HICSS 2024)](https://aisel.aisnet.org/hicss-57/da/data_science/10/): incorporates intervals between consecutive interactions into GRU gates to model changing short-term preferences. Earlier [Time-aware Attentive Memory Network (2020)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598) similarly uses a time-aware GRU for short-term intent and historical memory for longer-term interests, supporting dot-product recommendation. [DATA-GRU (AAAI 2020)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/5440), developed for irregular medical time series, provides another transferable mechanism: elapsed-time-dependent adjustment of the previous hidden state. These support learned temporal gating, but do not establish gains on this Amazon benchmark. A newer adjacent result, [GRUT (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.1300/), models timestamps and intervals in generative recommendation; its backbone and trend-based reranking do not fit the present GRU4Rec constraints.\n\nPractical design inference: retain one jointly trained GRU network per category; encode clipped log1p inter-event gaps and condition reset/update gates on item embeddings, prior state and gap features. A learned short-term state projection could decay with elapsed time while preserving a durable residual component. Compare against the corrected baseline using macro validation HR@10; temporal gating remains a hypothesis, not a guaranteed improvement. For padding invariance, skip state updates at padded positions, compute gaps only between real events, and read the final nonpadding position. Use observed history timestamps only; do not require the unknown next-event time. Preserve sequence-only compatibility through the host’s timestamp plumbing rather than guessing gaps from item IDs."}
